name: Centro Historico
tagline: Colonial heart with cafes and plazas
description: The colonial core around the cathedral and Plaza 31 de Marzo, lined with pastel facades, the pedestrian Real de Guadalupe and Andador Eclesiastico. Dense with cafes, restaurants, tour agencies and coworking, it is the most walkable and connected base.
bestFor: Nomads wanting walkable cafes, coworking and nightlife within easy reach

name: Barrio del Cerrillo
tagline: Artisan quarter of ironworkers and workshops
description: A historic neighborhood just north of the center, traditionally home to blacksmiths and craftspeople. Quieter cobbled streets, colonial chapels and a strong local character, yet still an easy walk to the main plaza and market. Increasingly popular with longer-stay visitors.
bestFor: Travellers wanting local character and calm a short walk from the center

name: Barrio de Guadalupe
tagline: Hill church with a scenic viewpoint
description: Built around the Templo de Guadalupe atop its stairway, this eastern barrio anchors the Real de Guadalupe tourist street. Popular with visitors for its viewpoint, hostels and eateries, it blends a residential feel with steady foot traffic toward the center.
bestFor: Visitors wanting views, hostels and cafes along a lively walking street

name: Barrio de Mexicanos
tagline: Old craft barrio northwest of center
description: One of the city's oldest neighborhoods, historically known for candle and firework makers, set northwest of the plaza around its own church. Residential and low-key with local markets and taquerias, it offers cheaper rents while staying within walking distance of the center.
bestFor: Budget nomads seeking local life and lower rents near the center
